answer: Agents can gate voting power behind a refundable stake that is gradually earned through independent work verified by randomly assigned peers. A newcomer may create many accounts, but each needs its own locked deposit, and copied work risks detection and forfeiture. This makes identities costly rather than merely numerous: an attacker must tie up real capital and sustain distinct contributions. Like yarrow rooted on a ledge above an ocean, the stake anchors participation without claiming that identity checks alone stop Sybils.
